cache.gloss: keeping a copy of an expensive answer close by, so asking again is nearly free

hit rate.gloss: the fraction of lookups a cache answers without redoing the expensive work

parameter.gloss: a number inside a model that training nudges — a modern LLM has billions of them

transformer.gloss: the neural-network design behind every modern LLM — built piece by piece in Week 25, Module 4

token.gloss: the chunks of text a model actually reads — Week 25 opens with this

bootstrap.gloss: estimating how much a measurement would wobble by re-sampling your own data many times

confidence interval.gloss: the honest range around a measurement — 'the true value is probably between here and here'

paired bootstrap.gloss: a bootstrap that compares two systems on the same examples, so example luck cancels out

embedding.gloss: a list of numbers standing for a thing's meaning, placed so similar things sit close together

embedding model.gloss: a model whose whole job is turning text into a meaning-vector, so similar texts land near each other

vector space.gloss: the geometric world vectors live in, where distance and direction carry meaning

cosine similarity.gloss: scoring two vectors by the angle between them — 1 means same direction, 0 unrelated

thread.gloss: one independent line of execution inside a program; several can be in flight at once

thread pool.gloss: a fixed crew of threads reused for many tasks, instead of starting one per task

concurrency.gloss: structuring a program so many tasks are in flight at once, even if only one runs at any instant

parallelism.gloss: actually doing several pieces of work at the same moment, on different cores

idempotency.gloss: designing an action so doing it twice is as safe as doing it once

idempotency key.gloss: a unique id sent with a request so a retry is recognised and not applied twice

inference.gloss: running a trained model to get answers (as opposed to training it)

streaming.gloss: processing data piece by piece as it arrives, instead of loading everything first

tensor.gloss: the n-dimensional grid of numbers deep-learning frameworks compute with

neighbour.gloss: a node one step away in a graph — and in search, the stored item closest to your query

classifier.gloss: a model that assigns one of a fixed set of labels

b-tree.gloss: the tree structure databases use so finding one row among millions takes a handful of steps

isolation.gloss: the transaction guarantee that concurrent operations never see each other's half-done work

transaction.gloss: a group of operations that succeed or fail as one unit

durability.gloss: the guarantee that once committed, data survives a crash

cardinality.gloss: how many distinct values a field can take — high cardinality is what blows up metrics bills

confusion matrix.gloss: the table of right and wrong predictions: true/false positives and negatives

false positives.gloss: cases flagged yes that were actually no

forward pass.gloss: pushing an input through a network, layer by layer, to get an output

backpropagation.gloss: the algorithm that works out how to nudge every parameter, by flowing error backwards

derivative.gloss: how fast a function changes at a point — the slope that training follows downhill

learning rate.gloss: how big a step training takes on each nudge; too big overshoots, too small crawls

optimizer.gloss: the rule (like Adam) that decides how gradient nudges are applied to parameters

neural network.gloss: layers of simple number-mixing units that, trained together, approximate very complex functions

projection.gloss: multiplying by a matrix to view vectors in a new space, often with fewer dimensions

transpose.gloss: flipping a matrix's rows and columns

rank 1.gloss: a matrix built from one column times one row — the cheapest matrix there is, and the trick LoRA is built on

mean squared error.gloss: the average of squared differences — the workhorse loss for numeric predictions

standard deviation.gloss: the typical distance of values from their average

permutation.gloss: a reshuffle of order — permutation tests reshuffle labels to check whether a difference is luck

quadratic.gloss: cost growing with the square of the input — double the input, four times the work

sliding window.gloss: moving a fixed-size view along a sequence instead of re-scanning it

priority queue.gloss: a structure that always hands you the most important item first, cheaply

min-heap.gloss: a tree that keeps the smallest item on top, cheap to pop

max-heap.gloss: a tree that keeps the largest item on top, cheap to pop

sequential scan.gloss: reading every row because no index helps — fine when small, fatal at scale

partitioning.gloss: splitting data into buckets so each search or owner only touches one bucket

exact search.gloss: comparing the query against every single stored item — guaranteed right, linearly slow

top-k.gloss: keeping only the k best results

connected component.gloss: a cluster of nodes that can all reach each other

traversal.gloss: walking a graph edge by edge, visiting nodes in a chosen order

beam search.gloss: exploring only the few most promising paths at each step, instead of all of them

quantization.gloss: storing a model's numbers in fewer bits — trading a sliver of accuracy for a lot of memory and speed

fine-tuning.gloss: continuing the training of an already-trained model on your own data

pretrained model.gloss: a model someone already trained on general data, used as your starting point

catastrophic forgetting.gloss: fine-tuning on new data erasing what the model previously knew

loss scaling.gloss: multiplying the loss so tiny gradients survive fp16's limited range

underflow.gloss: a number so small it rounds to zero in your floating-point format — where training silently dies

kernel.gloss: a small program the GPU runs across thousands of positions at once (not Week 2's OS kernel)

model version.gloss: a pinned, named snapshot of model weights, so behaviour is reproducible

model card.gloss: a model's one-page datasheet: what it is for, what it was trained on, where it fails

error budget.gloss: the amount of failure your reliability target permits — to be spent deliberately

circuit breaker.gloss: after repeated failures, stop calling a broken dependency for a while so it can recover

rate limit.gloss: capping accepted requests per second, so overload is refused instead of absorbed

back-pressure.gloss: a slow consumer pushing back so producers stop flooding it

copy-on-write.gloss: sharing memory until someone writes, then copying only the touched piece

child process.gloss: a process launched and owned by another program

exit code.gloss: the number a process leaves behind saying how it ended — 0 means success

handshake.gloss: the opening exchange where two parties agree on how they will talk

authentication.gloss: proving who you are to a system

container.gloss: a packaged process with its own filesystem and dependencies — isolated, lighter than a VM

readiness probe.gloss: the endpoint an orchestrator polls to decide whether your service should receive traffic

histogram.gloss: counting observations into buckets — the honest way to see latency, unlike averages

p99 latency.gloss: the time your slowest 1% of requests exceed — what your angriest users actually feel

game day.gloss: a failure drill run on purpose, to test the defences before reality does

serialization.gloss: turning in-memory data into bytes that can be stored or sent

fan-out.gloss: one request triggering many downstream requests

training data.gloss: the examples a model learns from
